name: Princeton University
character: The 600-acre main campus features Collegiate Gothic buildings, 17 distributed gardens, outdoor sculptures, and Lake Carnegie along its southern edge.

landmarks.name: Nassau Hall
landmarks.quote: Nassau Hall is the oldest building on campus.
landmarks.look: Historic campus hall with front entrance flanked by two bronze tigers.

landmarks.name: Lake Carnegie
landmarks.quote: At the southern edge of the campus is Lake Carnegie, an artificial lake named for Andrew Carnegie.
landmarks.look: Artificial lake at the southern edge of campus with a rowing center.

landmarks.name: Firestone Library
landmarks.quote: with the construction of Firestone Library in 1948
landmarks.look: Large university library building, plain if unknown.

landmarks.name: Princeton University Art Museum
landmarks.quote: the Princeton University Art Museum was not officially established until 1882
landmarks.look: University art museum building, plain if unknown.

landmarks.name: Cannon Green
landmarks.quote: To the south of Nassau Hall lies a courtyard that is known as Cannon Green.
landmarks.look: Courtyard south of Nassau Hall with a cannon buried in the center.

landmarks.name: Princeton Stadium
landmarks.quote: between Peyton and Fine halls next to Princeton Stadium and the Lewis Library.
landmarks.look: University stadium next to Lewis Library, plain if unknown.

landmarks.name: Lewis Library
landmarks.quote: Several prominent architects have contributed some more recent additions, including Frank Gehry (Lewis Library)
landmarks.look: Modern library building designed by Frank Gehry.

landmarks.name: Whig Hall
landmarks.quote: A second "Little Cannon" is buried in the lawn in front of nearby Whig Hall.
landmarks.look: Campus hall with a lawn in front holding a buried cannon.
